function: Joint learned control of UAV trajectory, ground-terminal power, subchannel allocation and discrete phase shifts of multiple RISs in a relay link, maximizing sum rate (p. 7).
system: UAV, ground terminals, BS: one omnidirectional antenna each; I=J=2 passive reflecting RISs, M=64 elements, 6-bit phases; OFDMA, 1 MHz subchannels; carrier band not stated (pp. 2-3, 11-12).
method: Soft actor-critic deep reinforcement learning (SAC-CATDPS) with twin critics and adaptive entropy temperature, trained online by interaction with a simulated environment and replay buffer (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: probabilistic LoS/NLoS path loss with Rician fading, 300 m x 300 m urban area; same simulator trains and tests; no dataset or measurements (pp. 4, 11).
test_conditions: Trained and tested in one simulated environment (30 test runs); sweeps of path loss, CSI error, RIS count, power show own training curves; no unseen scenario (p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned: no RIS, random phases, fixed phases, fixed trajectory (other parts still SAC); learned: DDPG, TD3, PPO applied to the same joint problem (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Average sum rate (Mb/s) of ground terminals, cumulative reward convergence, QoS satisfaction times per terminal, UAV trajectory maps (pp. 12-15).
complexity: Training complexity of actor and critic networks given as O(B×E×K×[...]) in layer sizes; no FLOPs, parameter count or measured runtime reported (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "the Rician fading model with a factor"; custom LoS-probability plus Rician simulator with parameters in Table I (p. 11). No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is mentioned, so a standard channel is missing.
q2_support: p. 12: "converging with more iterations under all path loss conditions"; each sweep (path loss, CSI uncertainty, RIS count, power, subchannels) shows its own training curves or is a parameter sweep, and no model trained in one scenario is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 12: "The DDPG algorithm [28] performs the joint" design (TD3 and PPO likewise); p. 13: "to SAC-CATDNPS, SAC-CATDRAPS, and SAC-CATDFPS" (no RIS, random and fixed phase shifts); all compared on sum rate.
q4_support: p. 10: "we derive the network complexities for the actor as O(B"; order of training complexity of actor and critic networks in layer sizes (Section III-D1).
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulation is carried out on an Ubuntu 20.04 server"; channels are simulated from the Table I parameters, and the paper gives no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: Area 6 rather than 3: the DRL agent jointly controls aerial-link power, subchannel allocation and RIS phase shifts (area 6 wins as more specific) together with UAV trajectory, so it passes above_phy (p. 7, actions). q3: the non-learned baselines (random or fixed RIS phases, fixed trajectory, no RIS) are SAC variants in which only the ablated part is non-learned, while DDPG, TD3 and PPO are standard DRL algorithms on the same problem (pp. 11-12); reviewer to confirm. q1: the LoS probability sigmoid with a=9.6, b=0.16 (Eq. 7, Table I) is a literature air-to-ground model, neither 3GPP nor measured. Complexity concerns training only (p. 10).
